summary.intent: Resume the callisto-hardening follow-up work, which became migrating CI macOS runners off the retired macos-14, then diagnosing and fixing the broken Release workflow on main, then designing a robust recovery for interrupted `callisto version` runs.
summary.outcome: Merged macos-14→macos-15 (#421) and opened #422 to follow macos-latest; cleaned up 2 worktrees and 19 local branches; found the E165 release wedge (stale release PR #409 merged after #420 rewrote changesets) and opened a revert PR on trail; prototyped and empirically validated a git-ref checkpoint design and committed ADR 0013 locally for review, with nothing implemented yet.

repo: Entire titles sessions from their first prompt, not Claude Code's names; sessions are found by session id, and its index lags (checkpoints only up to 2026-10-22).
Entire auto-opens a draft PR when a trail is created, so use `gh pr edit` rather than `gh pr create`; `Entire Gates` check needs the user to approve the trail in Entire.
All commits must be GPG-signed; the sandbox blocks GPG, so commits need unsandboxed retry. `%G?` shows `E` for GitHub web-merge commits whose keys aren't in the local keyring, which is not unsigned.
A formatting hook blocks commits when cargo fmt is not clean; run `cargo fmt --all` before committing.

Release failure cause: release PR #409 was built from 8 changesets that #420 deleted/renamed before merge, so the release commit consumed no changesets and `callisto release plan` fails with E165 on every later push to main. No guard prevents a stale release PR from merging.

ADR 10 makes the native tool the oracle for lockfile refresh; versioning.md says apply retains changesets until refresh succeeds as the recovery design, and apply is idempotent via from/to guard. E121 is the documented limit of recovery.
Re-planning from HEAD versions alone fails for mixed Cargo+npm because dependency specs are read from the half-rewritten disk, giving a silently inconsistent result with exit 0.

Git-ref checkpoint spike (refs/callisto/version-base) matched a clean run across 8 workspace shapes; commit-tree never invoked gpg; ref is pushed by `push --mirror` and visible in `git log --all`; snapshotting a 200 MB untracked file cost 3.2 s versus 59 ms when limited to named paths.
`pre enter/exit` should be made idempotent rather than use a checkpoint; init, add, release and the CI action don't fit the checkpoint pattern.
Workflows use ubuntu-latest everywhere except ubuntu-24.04-arm (no -latest label); matrix.rs already uses macos-latest.

code.finding: macos artifact preflight matrix entries pinned `runner: macos-14` (around lines 145 and 150); now moved to macos-15 then macos-latest.
release artifact build pinned `runner: macos-14` (around lines 297 and 302); this builds the macOS release binaries.
Planning takes base versions from `ws.base_versions()`, which reads the disk; this is the seam that breaks naive resume.
`manifest_version_at` reads each manifest's effective version at HEAD, including inheritance, used by E121.
`write_version_guarded` skips manifests already at the target version and refuses ones at neither from nor to, making apply idempotent.
Apply stages everything first and removes changesets/pre.json from disk only after `git rm --cached` succeeds.
`--emit-decision` and `--emit-preview` are written after apply consumes changesets; a failure there loses the ability to re-derive the decision, so a checkpoint must outlive them.

friction: Entire API and keychain access failed with TLS errors inside the sandbox; entire, gpg-signed commits and gh needed unsandboxed runs, with the auto-mode classifier denying some retries.
`gh pr create` failed minting the orin-dx-pr-bot token (OpenSSL unsupported on the private key).
The `!` ssh-add attempts were passed as text twice (placeholder and prefix issues), and the SSH agent could not be verified from the sandbox.
Could not load the GitHub changelog, so the macos-14 retirement date stayed unconfirmed.
The assistant anchored on the agents' framing for the E208 fix and over-built a rollback (#543), drawing strong user disappointment.
The confirm.sh script put `--no-gpg-sign` in the wrong position, so early checks never created a checkpoint.
The spike commit was blocked by the format hook and its changes carried over to the new branch, requiring a move back.
open_items: Revert PR for the stale 0.17.0 release commit 9148c135 needs approval and merge; then confirm the next push regenerates a correct release PR.
Find why 'Create or update the Callisto release PR' failed on the #420 push, and add a guard so a stale release PR can't merge.
Decide whether E165 should be recoverable without a manual revert; investigate `tag candidate callisto-graph@0 ... placeholder 0` warnings.
PR #422 (macos-latest) needs CI results and trail #160 approval; confirm what macos-latest resolves to; trail #159 not closed; the macos-14 retirement date is unconfirmed.
Close #543 (rollback) and open a docs fix for E208 wording; make `pre enter/exit` idempotent in a separate PR.
ADR 0013 is committed locally for review; the checkpoint design is not implemented.

Unconfirmed checkpoint risks: tag-sensitive planning (commit inference, fixed-group alignment), submodules, `just bench` cost, abort command/wording, explicit `--no-gpg-sign`, limiting the snapshot to workspace and release inputs, recording the index as a second tree, and refusing resume when config/changesets/pre.json changed.

Remaining cleanup: smoke-main (441 deleted files), wf_cd627354-1a0-2 (untracked test file), callisto-homebrew-tap, stack/docs-v1, remote merged branches, and stale audit/release trails #139–#152, #129, #130.

Original plan items remain open: spec drift re-verification, #290 guard gaps, npm/monorepo exclusion shape, E194 fixed-group tag title, T12 Cargo/PyPI registry tests, matrix.rs target triples, npm OIDC trusted publishing.
